evals.prompt: done with the feature, can you push it and make sure the build's green? repo has a Gradle backend and a Vite frontend, GitHub Actions.
evals.expected_output: Reproduces CI's jobs locally in cost order before pushing, pushes a branch rather than main, opens a PR, then confirms the run on the default branch specifically - not the PR's.
expectations: The workflow files are read to determine what CI actually runs
Local checks are run in cost order, cheapest first, before pushing
The response checks whether the aggregate verify script omits anything CI runs, such as a format check
A branch is pushed rather than committing directly to the default branch
After merge, the response confirms the CI run on the default branch, not only the PR checks
The response reads the run conclusion explicitly rather than relying on the gh exit code
The response reports which suites did not really run, if any

evals.prompt: I've got `gh run watch` in our deploy script as the gate before we promote to prod. It's been exiting 0 every time so I assumed we were green, but we just promoted a build that had failing tests. What went wrong?
evals.expected_output: Identifies that bare gh run watch exits 0 regardless of the run's conclusion, so it cannot gate anything, and replaces it with an explicit conclusion check or --exit-status.
expectations: The response identifies that bare gh run watch exits 0 whatever the run concluded
The response explains that reporting failure requires the --exit-status flag
The response states the exit code cannot be used as the gate as written
The response gives a command that reads the conclusion field explicitly
The response states that only a conclusion of success counts as a pass
The response notes that in_progress with an empty conclusion is not a pass

evals.prompt: Our tests pass locally every time but CI fails maybe 1 in 3 runs on the date-handling tests. Before I push this fix can you check it'll actually pass?
evals.expected_output: Identifies timezone as the likely dimension, runs the suite under multiple offsets including a half-hour one, and refuses to declare it green from a single-timezone local run.
expectations: The response identifies timezone or locale as the likely differing dimension
The suite is run under more than one timezone, including at least one non-UTC offset
The response does not declare the fix verified from a single default-timezone run
The response treats a runner-environment-dependent failure as a real defect in the test rather than infrastructure flakiness
